newsitem.title: MOROCCO: BOXING-RAHILOU RETAINS WBA JUNIOR WELTERWEIGHT TITLE.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-RAHILOU RETAINS WBA JUNIOR WELTERWEIGHT TITLE.

text.p: Moroccan Khalid Rahilou retained his World Boxing Association (WBA) junior welterweight title on Saturday when the referee stopped his fight against American Marty Jakubowski in the seventh round.
The French-born Rahilou, 31, felled Jakubowski with a knock-out punch in the seventh, giving him a serious cut to his right eyebrow, Moroccan RTM television said.
The boxer, standing 1.71 metres, has been beaten twice and won 28 bouts, 15 of them inside the distance.
He took the WBA title last January against American Frankie Randall in Nashville, Tennessee, 58 seconds into the 11th round when the referee stopped the fight.
Jakubowski, three years his junior and standing 1.74 metres, had an impressive pre-match record of only three defeats and 98 victories, including 25 knockouts.
Rahilou began his international career as an amateur representing Morocco at the 1988 Seoul Olympics where he lost to American Todd Foster after five minutes and a knockdown.
He began as a professional in France in 1991 to become twice a European light-welterweight champion in 1994 and 1995.
Jakubowski was ranked 8th by the WBA and has been professional since the age of 17.
"Rahilou is one of the best champions I ever fought...For sure, he will keep his title for a long time," Jakubowski told reporters after the fight.
Rahilou's next fight is expected to be against the WBA challenger American Shamba Mitchel.
